overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: no private deliberation with the Executive Director, the two-member exchange was not a quorum, and the chair lawfully limited public comment, though encouraging participation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Authority secretly deliberated with its Executive Director in her office before the February 15 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence to the contrary, we credit the Authority’s account of the facts and find that it did not have a private discussion with the Executive Director outside of a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a communication between two members about a member's phone call from the complainant was an improper deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: the communication was between two Authority members, which is not a quorum of the Authority.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair restricted the complainant's and another resident's participation during public comment at the February 15 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law therefore gives discretion to the chair of a public body to determine who may speak or otherwise participate at a meeting, and to set limits on public participation.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
